q: I lost my belongings after a concert. What should I do?
a: Check the Lost & Found notices on the Olympic Park website, or visit/call an Olympic Park Info Center: Peace Plaza Info Center (02-2180-3564~5) or Meeting Plaza Info Center (02-2180-3566).

q: How long does the park keep found items?
a: Items found in Olympic Park are kept at the Info Center for about one month from the date they were found. After that they are handed over to the local police station under the Lost Articles Act. Info Center hours: 09:00-19:00 (break 12:00-13:00). Storage: Meeting Plaza Info Center and Peace Plaza Info Center.

q: Where are the Info Centers and how can I call them?
a: Olympic Park has two Info Centers that keep found items: Peace Plaza Info Center (02-2180-3564~5) and Meeting Plaza Info Center (02-2180-3566). Hours: 09:00-19:00 (break 12:00-13:00).

q: What are the park's opening hours?
a: On foot or by bicycle: 5 a.m. to 10 p.m. (Peace Plaza and Meeting Plaza until midnight). By car: 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. (except during night events). After 10 p.m. entry to the inner park is closed except the two plazas.

q: How do I get to Olympic Park by public transport?
a: Subway: Olympic Park Station (Lines 5 and 9) Exit 3, or Mongchontoseong Station (Line 8) Exit 1. Many city and Gyeonggi buses stop at the gates; airport buses 6300 (East Gate 2) and 6006/6006-1 (Olympic Hall area).
There are 13 outdoor restrooms, including at Peace Plaza, Meeting Plaza, Mongchon Fortress and around the arenas. Maps are available at the security booths at each entrance.
The park has parking for about 2,800 cars, with five pay booths at North Gate 2, East Gate 2, South Gate 2, South Gate 3 and South Gate 4.

Parking is paid on exit: 600 won per 10 minutes for regular cars, 1,200 won per 10 minutes for large vehicles. Compact, disabled, national merit, low-emission and multi-child vehicles get 50% off. Re-entry is charged again.

q: How long does parking take on show days?
a: Traffic around the park is heavy just before shows. Allow about one hour, and use public transport if possible.
Outdoor kiosks open 10:00-18:00. The main store in front of the Handball Stadium opens 08:00-22:00. Other kiosks may change hours depending on events, weekends and holidays.

Personal drone flights are not allowed in Olympic Park for safety reasons. Event organizers may fly drones only with government approval.
Olympic Park has been a non-smoking park since November 2009.

q: Where can I get first aid?
a: Convenience stores sell bandages. Basic first-aid supplies are also kept at the Peace Plaza Info Center (02-2180-3564~5) and the Meeting Plaza Info Center (02-2180-3566).
